body.text: A Series is a one-dimensional labeled array capable of holding any data type (integers, strings, floats, objects). Each value has an associated label called an index.

body.code:

print(s)

questions.explanation: Missing values and duplicates are usually addressed early, before finalizing types.

questions.question: Which method is commonly used to clean inconsistent text formatting?
questions.explanation: String methods clean up whitespace and capitalization inconsistencies.

questions.question: Why convert a Marks column with pd.to_numeric(errors='coerce') during cleaning?
options: To safely turn invalid text entries into NaN instead of crashing the script
To convert it into a date
questions.explanation: This step gracefully handles unexpected non-numeric values in the raw data.

questions.question: What is typically the LAST step of a cleaning workflow?
questions.explanation: The workflow usually ends by exporting the cleaned dataset with to_csv()/to_excel().

questions.question: Why is a repeatable cleaning script more valuable than manual one-off fixes?
options: It can be rerun automatically whenever new raw data arrives
It removes the need for any inspection
questions.explanation: Automation makes the cleaning process consistent and reusable.

questions.question: Which method verifies that missing values have actually been handled after cleaning?
questions.explanation: Re-checking info()/isnull().sum() confirms the cleaning worked as intended.

questions.question: Which combination of steps best describes 'renaming for clarity' in a cleaning workflow?
options: Using df.rename(columns={...}) to give columns clear, consistent names
Using df.merge() to add new columns
questions.explanation: Renaming columns improves readability and consistency across the cleaned dataset.

chapters.title: Day 30: Capstone Project - Full Analysis Pipeline

body.text: The capstone combines everything learned over the past 29 days: loading data, cleaning it, transforming it, aggregating it, and visualizing the results — a complete, realistic analysis pipeline.

items: Clean: handle missing values, duplicates, and data types.
Transform: create new calculated columns (e.g. Total, Percentage, Grade).
Aggregate: use groupby()/pivot_table() to summarize by category.
Merge: combine with a second related dataset if available.
Visualize: produce at least 2 charts summarizing key findings.
Export: save the final cleaned/aggregated results to CSV or Excel.

body.text: A strong capstone tells a clear story: what question you asked, how the data was cleaned, what you found, and how the visuals support your conclusion.

body.title: Capstone Project
steps: Choose or create a realistic dataset (student records, sales data, etc.).
Run it through the full clean -> transform -> aggregate pipeline.
Merge in a second dataset if one is available.
Produce at least two charts summarizing your findings.
Export a final summary table to CSV or Excel.
Write a short 3-5 sentence summary of what the data shows.

questions.question: What is the goal of the capstone project?
options: To learn a single new function
To combine loading, cleaning, transforming, aggregating, and visualizing into one pipeline
questions.explanation: The capstone integrates the full range of skills covered over the 30 days.

questions.question: Which step in the suggested pipeline typically comes right after loading the data?
questions.explanation: Cleaning is generally performed early, right after the raw data is loaded.

questions.question: Which pandas feature is used to summarize results by category in the capstone?
questions.explanation: Aggregation functions summarize the cleaned/transformed data by group.

questions.question: Which step allows combining the primary dataset with a second related dataset?
questions.explanation: merge()/concat() bring in related data from a second source.

questions.question: Which step communicates the key findings visually?
questions.explanation: Charts are the step that visually communicates insights from the analysis.

questions.question: Which method exports a final summary table for sharing or reporting?
questions.explanation: Export methods save the finished results outside of the Python session.

questions.question: What does a strong capstone project typically include besides code?
options: A short written summary of the question, method, and findings
Only a single chart with no context
questions.explanation: Communicating the story behind the analysis is as important as the code itself.

questions.question: Which named-aggregation example groups students by Department and computes both average marks and student count?
questions.explanation: This uses named aggregation to produce a clear per-department summary.

questions.question: Why is sort_values() often applied to a summary table at the end of an analysis?
options: To highlight the highest or lowest performing groups clearly
questions.explanation: Sorting the summary makes key patterns (top/bottom performers) immediately visible.
